hypotheses.rationale: The auth service exhibited elevated latency (p95 up to 67.2ms) and high database pool utilization (up to 34.3%), correlating with repeated timeouts and deadlines exceeded in api-gateway logs. This directly impacts api-gateway error rates, which spiked to 6.31%.
While orders service logs indicate queue-related issues, these are less directly linked to the api-gateway error rate spike compared to auth service issues.
No direct evidence of a configuration error in api-gateway was found. The error rate spike is more likely due to downstream service failures.

recommended_remediation: Scale up the auth service database connection pool.
Monitor and optimize auth service latency and database pool utilization.
Investigate potential misconfigurations in auth service connection handling.
report.summary: The investigation identified a spike in the api-gateway error rate (6.31%, ALR-001) during the scenario window. The root cause is highly likely to be connection pool exhaustion in the auth service, supported by elevated p95 latency (up to 67.2ms, MET-01386, MET-01478, MET-01846) and repeated timeouts/deadlines in api-gateway logs (LOG-01022, LOG-01030, LOG-01032, LOG-01035). The auth service's database pool utilization also spiked (up to 34.3%, MET-00011, MET-00080, MET-00655), reinforcing the hypothesis. Orders service queue issues (LOG-00875, LOG-00937) were less directly linked to the api-gateway error rate spike.
report.uncertainty: No direct logs of connection exhaustion in auth service were found, but latency and pool utilization metrics strongly support the hypothesis.
